subject: cicada killer wasp
title: This Wasp's Prey Is Too Heavy to Lift, So It Climbs a Tree and Glides

scenes.text: This wasp hunts prey too heavy to take off with. It still gets it home.
The female eastern cicada killer stings a cicada, paralyzing it but keeping it alive.
Her cicadas usually weigh about twice as much as she does, close to her limit for flight.
When she can't take off from the ground, she climbs a tree with it, then launches and glides toward her burrow.
Underground, an egg that will become a male gets one cicada. A future female usually gets two, because females grow bigger.
The big males patrolling the burrows look scary. They can't sting at all.

description:
The female eastern cicada killer paralyzes a cicada, often about twice her own mass, and carries it to her burrow. When she can't fly with it from the ground, she climbs a tree or shrub and glides part of the way.
Each cell in the burrow gets one cicada for a male egg and usually two for a female egg. Males have no sting.
Would you have guessed the scary-looking males are harmless?
first_comment: About 2.5 times her own weight seems to be the most a female can carry in flight. Have you seen these giant wasps in your yard?
